name: Play Integrity verdicts
plain: Google returns a signed verdict on the device, app, and account integrity.
meaning: Verdict levels (BASIC, DEVICE, STRONG) tell servers if a phone is rooted, an emulator, or running an altered app. STRONG (Android 13+) needs hardware-backed signals and a recent patch.

android.note: MEETS_BASIC_INTEGRITY, MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY, MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY; STRONG needs a security patch within the last 12 months

limits.headline: Can ask Google whether the phone and app look genuine and unmodified
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you sign in, pay, or do something the app wants to protect
can: Ask Google for a signed verdict on the device, the app, and the Play license
See whether the phone passes basic, device, or strong integrity
Block actions on rooted, emulated or tampered devices
cannot: See who you are or your Google account details
See other apps on your phone
Give a strong verdict if the security patch is older than about 12 months
Work on iPhone; App Attest does that job
limits.reach_label: A verdict about the device and app
limits.differs: Only Android has Play Integrity. iPhone uses App Attest.

story.what_it_is: Google tells a server whether the phone, the app and the account look genuine.

marketing.name: Play Integrity API
marketing.pitch: Google helps apps detect risky or fake devices and apps so they can fight fraud, cheating and abuse.

story.for_you: You never see it. It runs in the background when you log in, buy something or play online. It can make a game or bank app refuse to run on a rooted phone or a custom system.
story.for_makers: Makers get a signed answer from Google about whether the device is real, the app is untouched and it was installed from Google Play. They use it to cut cheaters, bots and card fraud. It also locks out some honest users with custom software.

use_cases.example: A shooter checks the phone before a ranked match so cheat tool users are blocked.
A bank app refuses to open on a rooted phone, because malware could read the screen.
A payments app verifies the device before it approves a high value transfer.
A sale app limits scripted bots grabbing limited stock by checking each request.
A streaming app uses it to block pirated, repackaged copies of the app.
A new sign up is checked for emulators so one person cannot create thousands of fake accounts.

story.android_note: This is the Google service for Android, and the strongest verdict needs a recent security update and hardware signals.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no version. Apps use Apple App Attest for the same job.

history.change: Strong verdict requires hardware-backed boot signals and recent patch
